title: Localization of the native open tensor representatives
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and an open immersion $j:U\to Z$ between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Use the native framework of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], tensor and K-flat predicates of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations], generic presentations of [def-sf-generic-open-tensor-presentation], concrete operations of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-operations], and native comparison data of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-presentation-data]. For every native sheaf tensor datum $s$, there exist natural derived restriction/tensor and open tensor isomorphisms $\rho,\gamma$ and an OpenTensorPresentation $c$. Its extension, restriction, sheaf tensors, total tensors, derived tensors, K-flat predicates, tensor models and summand insertions are exactly the actual native ones. Its sheaf comparisons equal those of $s$, and its derived comparisons equal $\rho,\gamma$. All chain summand and K-flat representative normalization squares are those required by OpenTensorPresentation. In Lean these comparisons are pinned by eighteen heterogeneous equalities. No unit-transpose or ordinary-forgetting conclusion is included.

proof.text: Apply the fixed sheaf comparisons s.sheafGamma and s.sheafRestriction and their inverses in every bidegree, with the actual native tensor and open operations. The signed differential on degree (p,q) is dx tensor y + (-1)^p x tensor dy in both orders. Coproducts are created by forgetting Weil structures. Hence the maps assemble to chain isomorphisms whose every summand is the prescribed sheaf map. The ordinary total-complex theorem gives exactly this direct-sum convention.

proof.text: Use the equivariant flat-term K-flat resolution theorem on the twisted action site. Its finite-subextension coefficients agree with the native locally-finite-span coefficient functions: finitely many spanning values generate a finite subextension, and a quasi-compact test object requires finitely many neighborhoods. Their finite compositum gives the identification. By the K-flat preservation fields of s, extension and restriction send these resolutions to K-flat representatives of the exact open functors.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; native resolution and coefficient identification by Q85

proof.text: Check flat-term preservation too. For a flat sheaf on the open, restrict an ambient short exact sequence, tensor with that sheaf, and extend; the fixed sheaf comparison identifies this with tensor by its extension. For a flat ambient sheaf, extend a short exact sequence on the open, tensor with the ambient sheaf, and restrict back using the invertible unit in s; its restriction is flat. Thus both functors preserve the resolving subcategories. Apply ringed action-site derived tensor descent and the localization universal property to the chain maps and their inverses. Under the prescribed native tensor models and exact-functor factors, obtain rho and gamma and both representative squares. Naturality, resolution independence and the inverse identities descend in each variable. Set every other presentation field to the actual native construction, so its heterogeneous compatibility equalities are reflexive.

lean.statement:
theorem native_open_tensor_localization (s : NativeOpenTensorData k₀ l j) :
    ∃ (rho : nativeDerivedTensor k₀ l Z ⋙ nativeOpenPull k₀ l j ≅
        (nativeOpenPull k₀ l j).prod (nativeOpenPull k₀ l j) ⋙ nativeDerivedTensor k₀ l U)
      (gamma : nativeOpenDerivedLeft k₀ l j ≅ nativeOpenDerivedRight k₀ l j)
      (c : OpenTensorPresentation (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l U) (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l Z)),
      HEq c.E (extensionByZero k₀ l j) ∧ HEq c.R (upperStar k₀ l j) ∧
      HEq c.SA (nativeOpenSheafTensor k₀ l U) ∧ HEq c.SB (nativeOpenSheafTensor k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.TA (nativeTensorTotal k₀ l U) ∧ HEq c.TB (nativeTensorTotal k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.DA (nativeDerivedTensor k₀ l U) ∧ HEq c.DB (nativeDerivedTensor k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.flatA (NativeIsKFlat k₀ l U) ∧ HEq c.flatB (NativeIsKFlat k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.modelA (nativeOpenTensorModel k₀ l U) ∧
      HEq c.modelB (nativeOpenTensorModel k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.iA (nativeOpenTensorInsertion k₀ l U) ∧
      HEq c.iB (nativeOpenTensorInsertion k₀ l Z) ∧
      HEq c.sheafGamma s.sheafGamma ∧ HEq c.gamma gamma ∧
      HEq c.sheafRestriction s.sheafRestriction ∧ HEq c.restriction rho
